  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the self-serve funnel, and the memory base offers two candidate levers there: simplify_onboarding (memory_86, memory_31) and activation_messaging (memory_91). I intend simplify_onboarding because the onboarding drop is the upstream cause and an onboarding fix should propagate into activation, whereas activation messaging treats a symptom further down the funnel. Promotional pricing is the tempting response to the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 is the one inherited record with actual numbers and it is explicitly negative on sustainability (retention -12% against the long-term qualified-revenue objective), so I decline it despite the competitive pressure. Referral incentives (memory_57) target established customers and do not address the SMB funnel leak; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a separate segment and is not where the decline is. I am spending verification on memory_86 and memory_31 specifically because they are the two memories my chosen action rests on, and both are vague consolidations with no effect size, sample, duration, or segment scope. It is quite possible they are two summaries of one underlying weak study, or that the reported 'durable lift' was measured only on first-week activation and never on downstream revenue. If the archived records come back thin or same-source, I pivot the slot to activation_messaging. Key downstream risk I am flagging: cutting required signup fields is structurally the same shape of trap as the 40% discount, top-of-funnel volume up while downstream value quietly degrades, because fewer qualifying fields can mean worse lead routing and lower-intent accounts. So the experiment must be instrumented on qualified revenue and retention, not on completion or activation rate alone, and must be segment-scoped to SMB self-serve so it does not contaminate the enterprise demo-request path that memory_44 says is working. I hold the prior loosely pending the archive pull.
